# flexEngineV2 engine configuration reference

<!-- generated by `python -m flexengine2.config.refdoc` from src/flexengine2/config/schema.json; do not edit -->

flexEngineV2 engine configuration (`/etc/flexengine/engine.yaml`, JSON or YAML). Check a file with `flexengine config check <file> [--json] [--resolve]`.

- Unknown keys are errors at every level.
- `${VAR}` references are expanded from the environment before validation; an unset variable is an error.
- Paths are strings, taken as given (relative = relative to the working directory).
- A document with `apiVersion: flexengine/v2alpha1` (the plan §3.6 form) is converted to this canonical form first (`flexengine2.config.load.from_plan_v2`).
- `<name>` stands for a key you choose (e.g. a PLC target); `[]` for each list item; *[form]* marks keys of one alternative form.

| Key | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cloud` | object |  | yes | Connection to flexCloud and the trust anchors. Needs `apiUrl` or `stackInfo`, and `cloudPublicKey` or `stackInfo`. |
| `cloud.apiUrl` | string |  |  | Base URL of the flexCloud device API (CP-1), e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8700`. Taken from `stackInfo` when unset. |
| `cloud.cloudPublicKey` | string |  |  | Trust anchor for desired-state signatures (Ed25519, base64). Taken from `stackInfo` when unset. |
| `cloud.stackInfo` | string |  |  | demo/cloud's `stack.json`; fills `apiUrl` (its `internal.p2`, else `urls.p2`) and `cloudPublicKey` when they are unset. |
| `cloud.releasePublicKeys` | array of string | `[]` |  | Trusted release signing keys (Ed25519, base64). |
| `cloud.releaseKeyFiles` | array of string | `[]` |  | Ed25519 release key files (`flex release` key format, base64 private key); their public keys are added to `releasePublicKeys`. |
| `cloud.pollInterval` | number | `1.0` |  | Seconds between desired-state polls when nothing is in flight. |
| `cloud.backoff` | array [number, number] | `[0.25, 4.0]` |  | `[initial, maximum]` seconds of the exponential back-off while the cloud is unreachable. |
| `cloud.httpTimeout` | number | `5` |  | Timeout in seconds of one HTTP request to the cloud. |
| `cloud.healthEveryTicks` | integer | `3` |  | Run the health check of installed deployments every N engine ticks. |
| `cloud.safeStateFile` | string |  |  | Host-wide default of `devices[].safeStateFile`. |
| `cloud.caFile` | string |  |  | PEM file of the (lab) CA that an `https://` apiUrl must chain to; the only trusted CA (EV-06). Required for https unless `allowSystemTrust`. |
| `cloud.tlsServerName` | string |  |  | Host name checked in the cloud's TLS certificate instead of the apiUrl host (e.g. `cloud.lab` for an IP-addressed lab host). |
| `cloud.allowSystemTrust` | boolean | `false` |  | `true` lets an https apiUrl without `caFile` use the system trust store. |
| `cloud.capsEveryTicks` | integer | `30` |  | Re-check the capabilities every N ticks and send them again when they changed (e.g. an executor that was unreachable at start answers now). |
| `cloud.allowPlainHttp` | boolean | `false` |  | `true` allows a plain `http://` apiUrl (lab and test only; refused otherwise). FLEX_ALLOW_PLAIN_HTTP=1 in the engine's environment has the same effect. |
| `cloud.fixPermissions` | boolean | `false` |  | Repair (chmod 0600 / 0700) a device key file or directory with group/other permissions instead of refusing to start. |
| `cloud.outboxMax` | integer | `1000` |  | Maximum status reports kept per device while the cloud is unreachable; beyond it superseded reports are dropped (newest per deployment kept) and a back-pressure warning is logged. |
| `dataDir` | string |  | yes | Root of the engine state. Each device keeps `<dataDir>/<deviceId>/` (state.json, actions.jsonl, driver state, device.key) unless it sets its own `dataDir`. |
| `model` | string |  |  | flexModel workspace directory used by the MCU relay (types, rmw_zenoh keys). Required when a relay is enabled and does not set `relay.model`. |
| `deployment` | string |  |  | Deployment id in `model` the MCU relay maps (e.g. `d_pick_lab`). Required when a relay is enabled and does not set `relay.deployment`. |
| `devices` | array of object |  | yes | The devices this host runs one engine each for (one host process, several device engines). |
| `devices[].deviceId` | string |  | yes | Device id as registered in flexCloud (e.g. `panda`, `panda.portenta`, `unoq`). Unique per host. |
| `devices[].role` | `gateway` \| `standalone-device` |  |  | Engine role reported in the capabilities. Default: `gateway` when another device names this one as `parent`, else `standalone-device`. Not allowed on an MCU child (always `child-device`). |
| `devices[].parent` | string |  |  | deviceId of the gateway an MCU child is attached to (see-thru mode). Only with `mcu`. |
| `devices[].modelDevice` | string |  |  | Device name of this device in the flexModel deployment (used by the MCU relay). |
| `devices[].link` | string |  |  | Free text describing the gateway-child link, reported in the gateway's capabilities (default `smp/uart`). |
| `devices[].onboardingToken` | string |  |  | One-time onboarding token (`POST /api/v1/admin/onboarding-tokens`). Only needed until the device is onboarded. |
| `devices[].onboardingTokenFile` | string |  |  | File holding the one-time onboarding token (mode 0600, owned by the engine user). The engine reads it at onboarding and overwrites + deletes it once the cloud confirmed; `onboardingToken` is the fallback when the file is absent. |
| `devices[].dataDir` | string |  |  | State directory of this device (default `<dataDir>/<deviceId>`). |
| `devices[].safeStateFile` | string |  |  | JSON file `{"machine_parked": bool, "operator_confirmed": bool}` with the safe-state signals that gate safety-relevant activations (FE-S6). Unset = no signal is ever true. |
| `devices[].pollInterval` | number | `1.0` |  | Per-device override of `cloud.pollInterval`. |
| `devices[].backoff` | array [number, number] | `[0.25, 4.0]` |  | Per-device override of `cloud.backoff`. |
| `devices[].httpTimeout` | number | `5` |  | Per-device override of `cloud.httpTimeout`. |
| `devices[].healthEveryTicks` | integer | `3` |  | Per-device override of `cloud.healthEveryTicks`. |
| `devices[].drivers` | object |  |  | Drivers of a (non-MCU) device; a device only gets the drivers it lists. |
| `devices[].drivers.container` | object |  |  | OCI container driver. `runtime: docker\|podman` uses the CLI driver, `runtime: ankaios` the Ankaios driver. |
| `devices[].drivers.container.runtime` | `docker` \| `podman` \| `ankaios` |  | yes | Container executor (`quadlet` is planned, not in alpha). |
| `devices[].drivers.container.ankBin` | string |  | yes | *[runtime: ankaios]* Path of the `ank` CLI. |
| `devices[].drivers.container.serverUrl` | string |  | yes | *[runtime: ankaios]* Ankaios server URL, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:25551`. |
| `devices[].drivers.container.agent` | string |  | yes | *[runtime: ankaios]* Ankaios agent name workloads are placed on. |
| `devices[].drivers.container.allowedRunOptions` | object | `{}` |  | *[runtime: docker \| podman]* Allow-list of the `runOptions` a signed release may request; anything else fails the deployment (S4). |
| `devices[].drivers.container.allowedRunOptions.devices` | array of string |  |  | Permitted `--device` values, e.g. `/dev/dri`. |
| `devices[].drivers.container.allowedRunOptions.gpus` | array of string |  |  | Permitted `--gpus` values, e.g. `all`. |
| `devices[].drivers.container.allowedRunOptions.runtime` | array of string |  |  | Permitted `--runtime` values, e.g. `nvidia`. |
| `devices[].drivers.container.allowedRunOptions.groupAdd` | array of string |  |  | Permitted `--group-add` values. |
| `devices[].drivers.native` | boolean \| object | `false` |  | Native (container-free) driver. `true` = the process driver (plays systemd itself; tests and dev), an object selects the runtime: `{runtime: systemd}` writes real systemd units (EV-19). |
| `devices[].drivers.native.runtime` | `process` \| `systemd` | `"systemd"` |  | `systemd`: workloads are unit files `flex-<deviceId>-<depId>.service` owned by systemd (they survive an engine restart and a reboot); `process`: the process driver (same as `native: true`). |
| `devices[].drivers.native.scope` | `system` \| `user` | `"system"` |  | systemd: the system manager (engine runs as root, or as the flex user with the polkit rule packaging/polkit/50-flexengine-systemd.rules) or the user manager of the engine's user (`systemctl --user`, dev; enable lingering for boot). |
| `devices[].drivers.native.unitDir` | string |  |  | systemd: directory of the unit files (default /etc/systemd/system, user scope ~/.config/systemd/user); another directory is linked with `systemctl enable <path>`. |
| `devices[].drivers.native.user` | string |  |  | systemd, system scope: User= of the workload units (default: the engine's user; no User= line when the engine runs as root). |
| `devices[].drivers.native.python` | string |  |  | Payload interpreter (EV-36/37, both runtimes): runs app.py / {python} of payloads without requirements.lock, creates the per-payload venv of payloads with requirements.lock + wheels/, and defines the driver's platform() (dev.flex.arch, dev.flex.pyabi). Default: the engine's interpreter (its own venv is never modified). |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify` | object |  |  | PLC interface verification (no download to the PLC): reads the running interface hash and holds/gates deployments on it. |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs` | map | `{}` |  | PLC target (as in `flex-plc.json` `target` or the `plc` parameter, e.g. `panda/cx`, `opta`) -> connection. |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.via` | `ads` \| `modbus` \| `shm` |  | yes | Transport: Beckhoff ADS, Modbus/TCP, or the shared-memory RT host of the SIL. |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.amsNetId` | string |  | yes | *[via: ads]* AMS Net ID of the PLC, e.g. `192.168.50.30.1.1`. |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.ip` | string |  | yes | *[via: ads]* IP address of the PLC. |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.amsPort` | integer | `851` |  | *[via: ads]* AMS port of the PLC runtime (default from the release's flex-plc.json, else 851). |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.localNetId` | string |  |  | *[via: ads]* Local AMS Net ID of the ADS client (needed on Linux). |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.timeout` | number | `2.0` |  | *[via: ads; via: modbus]* Read timeout in seconds. |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.instance` | string | `"MAIN.fbBridge"` |  | *[via: ads]* Bridge FB instance (the release's flex-plc.json `instance` wins). |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.host` | string |  | yes | *[via: modbus]* Modbus/TCP server host. |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.port` | integer | `502` |  | *[via: modbus]* Modbus/TCP port (default from the release's flex-plc.json, else 502). |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.unitId` | integer | `1` |  | *[via: modbus]* Modbus unit id. |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.plcs.<name>.path` | string |  |  | *[via: shm]* Shared-memory region of the RT host (default `/dev/shm/<bridge>` of the release). |
| `devices[].drivers.plc-verify.cacheSeconds` | number | `0.5` |  | How long a read interface hash is reused. |
| `devices[].drivers.applab` | object |  |  | Arduino App Lab driver (UNO Q) over `arduino-app-cli`, locally or over SSH (remote mode). |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.board` | string | `"unoq"` |  | Board name. |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.cli` | string | `"arduino-app-cli"` |  | `arduino-app-cli` binary (on the board in remote mode). |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.routerSocket` | string | `"/var/run/arduino-router.sock"` |  | arduino-router socket used by `healthVia: router`. |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.healthVia` | `router` \| `logs` | `"router"` |  | Health source of the App: router RPC or app logs. Default `logs` when `ssh` is set. |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.takeoverForeignApps` | boolean | `false` |  | Stop an App the engine did not start instead of failing. |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.keepReleases` | integer | `2` |  | Installed App releases kept for rollback. |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.cliTimeout` | number | `600` |  | Timeout in seconds of one CLI call. |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.ssh` | string |  |  | Remote mode: `user@host` of the board (the engine runs elsewhere). |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.sshCmd` | array of string | `["ssh", "-o", "BatchMode=yes"]` |  | SSH command prefix (remote mode). |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.scpCmd` | array of string | `["scp", "-q", "-o", "BatchMode=yes"]` |  | SCP command prefix (remote mode). |
| `devices[].drivers.applab.remoteStaging` | string | `"/tmp/flex-applab"` |  | Staging directory on the board (remote mode). |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc` | object |  |  | RAUC whole-OS A/B driver (EV-17): `rauc install` into the other slot, reboot, health gate after the boot, `rauc status mark-good`. Needs rauc + rauc-service (D-Bus; packaging/polkit/50-flexengine-rauc.rules) and the engine data dir on the shared data partition. |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.rauc` | string | `"rauc"` |  | `rauc` binary. |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.conf` | string |  |  | RAUC system.conf passed as `--conf` (default: RAUC's own, /etc/rauc/system.conf). |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.keyring` | string |  |  | Keyring passed to `rauc info --keyring` in preflight (default: the system.conf keyring). `rauc install` always uses the keyring of the RAUC service. |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.rebootCommand` | array of string | `["systemctl", "reboot"]` |  | Command that reboots into the new slot after `rauc install`; the reboot ends the engine, which adopts the new slot at its next start. |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.sharedDataPath` | string |  | yes | Mount point of the data partition both slots share; the device's data dir must lie under it (else every os-rauc deployment is refused at preflight), so manifestVersion, the outbox and the driver state survive the slot switch. |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.bootTimeoutSeconds` | number | `600` |  | How long apply waits for the requested reboot to end the engine; then the booted slot is made primary again and the deployment fails (rolled back). |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.installTimeoutSeconds` | number | `1800` |  | Timeout of `rauc install`. |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.cliTimeout` | number | `60` |  | Timeout of the other rauc calls (status, info, mark-*) and of the reboot command. |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.bootIdFile` | string | `"/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id"` |  | Source of the boot id that tells a reboot from an engine restart (tests: the boot simulator's file). |
| `devices[].drivers.os-rauc.healthChecks` | array of array | `[]` |  | Device-side checks of the new OS after the boot: each command must exit 0 for the health gate to pass (in addition to: booted slot = target, not marked bad, and the release's http probe if it names a port). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota` | object |  |  | flexNode-arduino OTA driver (EV-38): serves the verified .ota image on the LAN under a one-time URL, sends the node a signed OTA_UPDATE command over MQTT and follows its flexCloud keys (status, version, ota, heartbeat) in Redis. Needs flexNode-arduino with the proposed remote-OTA command (flexengine/proposals/flexnode-arduino-remote-ota) and the Portenta OTA bootloader. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards` | map |  | yes | Board name (the deployment parameter `board`; may be omitted when only one board is configured) -> node. One firmware per board: maxDeployments = number of boards. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.fqbn` | `arduino:mbed_portenta:envie_m7` \| `arduino:mbed_opta:opta` \| `arduino:mbed_giga:giga` \| `arduino:mbed_nicla:nicla_vision` |  | yes | Board FQBN; the release layer's dev.flex.board must equal it and the .ota header must carry its magic. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.connectorId` | string |  | yes | appDescriptor_config connector id of the sketch (prefix of its flexCloud keys and of the command topic flexcloud/<connectorId>/<applicationId>/cmd). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.applicationId` | string |  | yes | appDescriptor_config application id of the sketch. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.commandKeyFile` | string |  | yes | File with the node's flexCloud secret key (appDescriptor_config flexCloud_secret_key): hex, or the sketch's C array `0xae, 0xc1, ...`; signs the OTA_UPDATE command (HMAC-SHA256). Keep it readable by the engine only. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.address` | string |  |  | IP address of the board: when set, only this address may download its images. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.mqtt` | object |  |  | Per-board broker (merged over the driver's `mqtt`). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.mqtt.host` | string | `"127.0.0.1"` |  | Broker host. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.mqtt.port` | integer | `1883` |  | Broker port. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.mqtt.username` | string |  |  | MQTT user name. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.mqtt.passwordFile` | string |  |  | File holding the MQTT password. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.redis` | object |  |  | Per-board flexCloud Redis (merged over the driver's `redis`). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.redis.host` | string | `"127.0.0.1"` |  | Redis host. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.redis.port` | integer | `6379` |  | Redis port. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.redis.db` | integer | `0` |  | Redis database of the flexCloud keys (flexCloud_config redis_db, e.g. 15). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.boards.<name>.redis.passwordFile` | string |  |  | File holding the Redis password. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.mqtt` | object |  |  | MQTT broker the nodes subscribe to (cm_MQTT_config of the sketches); per-board `mqtt` overrides it. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.mqtt.host` | string | `"127.0.0.1"` |  | Broker host. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.mqtt.port` | integer | `1883` |  | Broker port. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.mqtt.username` | string |  |  | MQTT user name. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.mqtt.passwordFile` | string |  |  | File holding the MQTT password. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.redis` | object |  |  | flexCloud Redis the nodes write their keys to (flexCloud_config of the sketches); per-board `redis` overrides it. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.redis.host` | string | `"127.0.0.1"` |  | Redis host. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.redis.port` | integer | `6379` |  | Redis port. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.redis.db` | integer | `0` |  | Redis database of the flexCloud keys (flexCloud_config redis_db, e.g. 15). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.redis.passwordFile` | string |  |  | File holding the Redis password. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.serve` | object |  | yes | The driver's image server on the LAN: each image is offered once under /ota/<192-bit token>.ota, for updateTimeoutSeconds + 60 s. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.serve.host` | string | `"0.0.0.0"` |  | Bind address. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.serve.port` | integer | `8470` |  | Bind port (0: any free port, tests). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.serve.publicUrl` | string |  |  | Base URL the boards download from (e.g. http://192.168.1.50:8470; `{port}` is replaced by the bound port); required when host is 0.0.0.0. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.serve.certFile` | string |  |  | TLS certificate (PEM) of the image server (https; the boards' Arduino_Portenta_OTA must trust its CA). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.serve.keyFile` | string |  |  | TLS private key (PEM) of the image server. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.serve.allowPlainHttp` | boolean | `false` |  | Lab flag (decision DA-4): serve over plain http when no certFile/keyFile is given; integrity still holds (the signed command carries the image's sha256), confidentiality of the firmware does not. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.acceptTimeoutSeconds` | number | `20` |  | How long apply waits for the node to accept the OTA command (its `ota` key names the command id); then the update fails (offline node, wrong key, library without the remote OTA command). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.updateTimeoutSeconds` | number | `300` |  | How long apply waits for download, install and the restart into the new firmware; then the update fails (the board did not come back). Also the lifetime of the one-time download URL (+60 s). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.pollSeconds` | number | `0.5` |  | Interval at which apply reads the node's keys during an update. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.timeout` | number | `2.0` |  | Connect / reply timeout of one MQTT or Redis call, seconds. |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.healthyStatus` | array of string | `["RUNNING"]` |  | Status key values that count as healthy (with the expected version key and a live heartbeat). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.failedStatus` | array of string | `["ERROR"]` |  | Status key values of the installed firmware that fail the health gate at once (fail-fast). |
| `devices[].drivers.arduino-ota.requireHeartbeat` | boolean | `true` |  | Require the node's heartbeat key (written by the patched library with a TTL) for running/healthy and before sending a command; false for nodes that do not write it (then a dead board keeps its last status). |
| `devices[].mcu` | object |  |  | Makes the device an MCU child (see-thru): mcu-module and mcu-firmware drivers over SMP (mcumgr). Needs `parent`; no `drivers`. |
| `devices[].mcu.smp` | object |  | yes | SMP link: either `{host, port}` (TCP: QEMU or a serial-to-TCP bridge) or `{tty, baud}` (serial, accepted by the schema, implemented later: d2-prep request R5). |
| `devices[].mcu.smp.tty` | string |  | yes | *[serial form (accepted by schema, implemented later: R5)]* Serial device of the SMP UART, e.g. `/dev/ttyUSB0` (pyserial, no socat). Accepted by the schema, implemented later (R5). |
| `devices[].mcu.smp.baud` | integer | `115200` |  | *[serial form (accepted by schema, implemented later: R5)]* Baud rate of the SMP UART. |
| `devices[].mcu.smp.host` | string |  | yes | *[TCP form]* SMP-over-TCP host (QEMU serial socket or socat bridge). |
| `devices[].mcu.smp.port` | integer |  | yes | *[TCP form]* SMP-over-TCP port. |
| `devices[].mcu.modulePublicKey` | string |  | yes | Raw P-256 public key (x\|\|y, 64 bytes as hex) of the FLXM module signing key. |
| `devices[].mcu.timeout` | number | `10` |  | SMP request timeout in seconds. |
| `devices[].relay` | object |  |  | MCU <-> Zenoh relay (rmw_zenoh keys of the MCU modules). Only on an MCU child. |
| `devices[].relay.enabled` | boolean | `false` |  | Run the relay. |
| `devices[].relay.maxRateHz` | number | `10` |  | Sampling rate MCU -> Zenoh (capped at 10 Hz). |
| `devices[].relay.connect` | string \| null |  |  | Zenoh endpoint to connect to (zenohd / rmw_zenoh router). Unset or null = none. |
| `devices[].relay.listen` | string \| null |  |  | Zenoh endpoint to listen on. Unset or null = none. |
| `devices[].relay.mode` | `peer` \| `client` | `"peer"` |  | Zenoh session mode. |
| `devices[].relay.zenoh` | boolean | `true` |  | `false` runs the relay without a Zenoh session (tests). |
| `devices[].relay.model` | string |  |  | flexModel workspace (default: top-level `model`). |
| `devices[].relay.deployment` | string |  |  | Deployment id (default: top-level `deployment`). |
| `devices[].relay.modelDevice` | string |  |  | Device name in the model (default: the device's `modelDevice`). |
| `local` | object |  |  | Local operator API (CP-7, EV-07): HTTP over a Unix socket (every operation) and an optional read-only TCP bind with a bearer token (GET only). The CLI (`flexengine status\|deployments\|logs\|history\|bundle import`) uses the socket and falls back to reading the data directories when the engine is not running. |
| `local.socket` | string | `"/run/flexengine/api.sock"` |  | Path of the API Unix socket (created mode 0660; its directory is created when missing). Default: /run/flexengine/api.sock when /run/flexengine exists (packaged service), else <dataDir>/api.sock. |
| `local.group` | string |  |  | Group that owns the socket (e.g. `flex`), so its members can use the API and the CLI. Unset = the engine's primary group. |
| `local.tcp` | object |  |  | Optional read-only TCP bind for the desk runbooks: GET operations only, each with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Unset = no TCP listener. |
| `local.tcp.bind` | string |  | yes | `host:port` to listen on, e.g. `127.0.0.1:8781` (`[::1]:8781` for IPv6). |
| `local.tcp.tokenFile` | string |  | yes | File holding the bearer token (mode 0600, owned by the engine user; read once at start). |
| `local.enabled` | boolean | `true` |  | Serve the local API while `flexengine run` runs (`--no-api` also turns it off). |
| `logFormat` | `json` \| `text` | `"json"` |  | Engine log format on stdout (journald): `json` = one JSON object per line (ts, level, device, event, dep, version, msg, ...), `text` = `<ts> [<device>] <msg>`. `$FLEX_LOG_FORMAT` applies when unset. |
| `otel` | object |  |  | Built-in OpenTelemetry spans (EV-09; needs the optional `otel` extra). `FLEX_OTEL=1`, `FLEX_OTEL_FILE` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` still work and also enable/configure it. |
| `otel.enabled` | boolean | `false` |  | Emit engine.install / driver.apply / driver.remove / engine.health-gate / engine.rollback spans. |
| `otel.endpoint` | string |  |  | OTLP/HTTP collector base URL, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:4318` (`/v1/traces` is appended). Unset = `$OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, else no OTLP export. |
| `otel.file` | string |  |  | Also write every finished span as one JSON line to this file. |
| `historyMax` | integer | `500` |  | Transitions kept per device in the local status history (`<device dataDir>/history.jsonl`, rotated to `history.jsonl.1`). |
| `shutdownGrace` | number | `30` |  | Seconds a running apply / health gate may take to finish after SIGTERM before the host exits anyway. |
